title: Man. Post. Cap. VII: GAR — judicial action at least for penalties; dying-you-die
pass_a_gloss: GAR grants for argument that losing justice needed no judicial act, yet says that by his fall Adam not only dropped justice but deserved to fall into calamities of every kind—so if one grants no judicial action for losing justice, one must at least confess that for undergoing penalties a judicial action ought to have intervened. That, he says, is chiefly what dying you shall die means.
pass_b_english: GAR. And since by his fall Adam not only fell from his justice but deserved to fall into calamities of every kind; if anyone acknowledges that for losing justice there was no need of a judicial action, he will at least confess that for undergoing penalties it ought to have intervened: for that is chiefly what dying you shall die means.
source_text: GAR. Et cum lapsu suo Adam non modo exciderit justitia sua, sed in omnigenas calamitates incidere commeruerit; si quis agnoscat ad justitiam amittendam nihil opus fuisse judiciaria actione, fatebitur saltem ad poenas subeundas eam intervenire oportuisse: hoc est enim praecipue illud morte morieris.

choices.choice: Even if no judicial for losing justice, need it for penalties / dying-you-die

notes: Cap. VII poena densify section 378 from locked 1661 Latin (pp. 265 tip–266 tip).
